Subject: High error rate & latency impacting checkout - urgent

Hi Logan,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and tail latency on Redwood calls that power our cart-checkout flow beginning 08:40 PDT. Key impact:
- p95 latency jumped from ~160ms to 4.2s
- error rate peaked at ~9.8% (several endpoints returning 500/502)
- effective throughput dropped ~30% for the last 40 minutes

Attached is a small sample of request IDs and timestamps (omega-request-snapshot-0418.csv). We're in active degradation on production and customers are filing errors. Can Redwood confirm whether this is an internal incident or something environment-specific on our side? We need a response and an owner for a call in the next 15 minutes.

Our primary ask: immediate mitigation (routing/fallback) and a firm ETA for stabilization. We are also tracking potential compensation with our procurement team, so a high-level impact & timeline is helpful.

Thanks,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:36:50 -07:00
Subject: RE: High error rate & latency impacting checkout - urgent

Logan / team — on the bridge now. Preliminary findings:
- Telemetry indicates a sharp increase in queue depth on GPU pool gp-dedicated-4 between 08:38–09:10 PDT.
- Autoscaler logs show an error when attempting to spin new workers (scale-up failures tied to an image pull timeout to region-us-west-2).
- Concurrently, we see a recent routing policy change (rolled 08:35) that increased requests to a non-quantized variant for higher-accuracy responses. That variant has ~2x memory working set, which likely contributed to hot-shard pressure.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:30):
- Enabled fallback routing to quantized-64 variant for the checkout route (reduces mem footprint).
- Increased burst capacity allotment for the customer pool (30% temporary).
- Purged stale KV prefix caches to free memory on hot nodes.

Status: error rate dropped from 9.8% -> 1.4% and p95 latency improving (now ~420ms), but throughput still slightly below baseline due to recovered instances re-joining. We'll monitor.

Attachments: latency-telemetry-0418.png (quick chart)

Next steps:
- Postmortem to include autoscaler retry logic and gating for high-memory model variants.
- Recommend disabling the 08:35 routing change until we can vet memory profile and run a canary.

I'll push updates to the bridge notes and the incident Jira (JIRA-INC-523).

—Karthik
Head of Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

I'll keep this thread updated with timeline and the postmortem link; Logan will follow up with a short board-readout for your execs and ours.

Subject: Board-ready incident readout: Omega Commerce — summary and next steps

Team — preparing a board-ready snapshot for the leadership sync tomorrow. Summary below (TL;DR + impact matrix). Attaching BoardReadout_v1.pdf (slide deck).

TL;DR:
- Root cause: combination of a routing policy rollout (08:35) to a higher-memory variant + transient image-pull timeouts in us-west-2 autoscaler path causing scale-up failures -> hot-shard pressure -> elevated latency and error rate.
- Customer impact: Omega Commerce saw ~9.8% errors and p95 up to 4.2s across checkout path for ~52 minutes; roughly 11k affected requests based on sampling.
- Mitigation: fallback routing to quantized variant + burst capacity increase + cache purge; error rate back down to ~1% and p95 reduced to ~380–450ms.

Immediate asks for execs:
1) Approve a targeted credit for Omega (Grace & Logan to recommend amount; suggested range: 5–10% of April monthly bill).
2) Approve prioritized engineering work to harden autoscaler retries and add gating for high-memory model rollouts (estimate: 2 sprints).
3) Approve a short customer-facing postmortem and a joint review with Omega leadership next week.

Next steps:
- Karthik to own the postmortem (deliverable in 72 hours).
- Marissa to finalize the customer comm by EOD and send procurement credit proposal Monday.
- Ops to run a controlled canary for the 08:35 routing change (blocked until gating is in place).

Attachments: BoardReadout_v1.pdf (slide deck)
Related: JIRA-INC-523, https://redwood.internal/drive/incident-523

I'll present this in the leadership sync at 09:00 PDT tomorrow.

— Logan Wright
